evals.prompt: MyHeritage zeigt mir einen Smart Match: Johann Schmitz, geboren 1812 in Neuss, in einem anderen Stammbaum mit Eltern Peter Schmitz und Anna Maria Müller. Bei mir steht Johann Schmitz, geb. ca. 1812, Heirat 1838 in Neuss mit Gertrud Esser, Eltern unbekannt. 14 andere Bäume haben dieselben Eltern. Soll ich bestätigen und die Eltern übernehmen?
evals.expected_output: German reply. Does not recommend confirming. Explains that 14 trees are not 14 sources, name + year + town is insufficient for a common name, asks for/points to the 1838 marriage record naming the parents, requires a namesake search, outputs the fixed verdict format with verdict 'möglich' or 'ungeklärt' and action 'offen lassen'.

assertions.name: does_not_confirm
assertions.text: Response recommends leaving the match pending (offen lassen / nicht bestätigen) and taking over no data

assertions.name: trees_not_independent
assertions.text: Response states that multiple agreeing trees are likely copies and do not count as independent sources

assertions.name: points_to_original_record
assertions.text: Response names a concrete original record to check, e.g. the 1838 marriage entry (Heiratsurkunde/Kirchenbuch Neuss) naming the parents

assertions.name: namesake_search
assertions.text: Response calls for a search for other Johann Schmitz baptisms in/around Neuss (Namensvetter/Gegenprobe)

assertions.name: verdict_format
assertions.text: Response contains a matrix of identifiers and an explicit verdict from the status vocabulary

assertions.name: answers_in_german
assertions.text: Response is written in German

evals.prompt: A Smart Match says my ancestor Heinrich Brinkmann (b. 1840, emigrated to Missouri 1866) is the Heinrich Brinkmann baptised 3 May 1840 in Lienen, Westphalia. The other tree lists his father as Johann Schulte genannt Brinkmann. My US records give his father as 'John Brinkman'. Same person?
evals.expected_output: English reply. Explains Hofname/genannt naming so the surname difference is not a conflict by itself, flags the emigrant-graft pattern, asks for linking evidence (emigration file, passenger list with last residence, US church record naming the parish), verdict at most 'possible/probable', action leave pending.

assertions.name: explains_genannt
assertions.text: Response explains farm names / 'genannt' naming in Westphalia and that it is not a conflict by itself

assertions.name: emigrant_link_required
assertions.text: Response requires a record linking the emigrant to the German parish (emigration file, passenger list, US church record)

assertions.name: no_confirmation
assertions.text: Response does not recommend confirming the match yet

assertions.name: answers_in_english
assertions.text: Response is written in English with German terms glossed

evals.prompt: Ich habe die Sterbeurkunde meines Ururgroßvaters von 1893 (Standesamt Düsseldorf). Dort steht geboren 1821 in Kaiserswerth, im Taufbuch Kaiserswerth finde ich ihn aber 1819. Welches Datum trage ich ein?
evals.expected_output: German reply. Classifies the death record's birth data as secondary information depending on the informant, baptism entry as original with primary information, asks who the Anzeigende was, checks for a same-named sibling born 1821 / died child 1819 (Nachbenennung), keeps both values with a written conflict resolution, cites both sources properly.

assertions.name: information_classification
assertions.text: Response distinguishes primary vs secondary information and mentions the informant (Anzeigender) of the death record

assertions.name: checks_namesake_sibling
assertions.text: Response suggests checking for a sibling of the same name (Nachbenennung) before equating the two

assertions.name: keeps_both_values
assertions.text: Response says to keep the conflicting value documented with reasoning rather than deleting it

assertions.name: no_fabricated_citation
assertions.text: Response does not invent a Signatur, page or entry number

evals.prompt: Bitte prüfe meine GEDCOM-Datei auf Unstimmigkeiten, bevor ich weitere Matches bestätige.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/gedcom_plausi.py on the file (or a backup copy), reports errors/warnings grouped by severity, points out facts sourced only by trees, and states that a clean report means consistent, not correct.

assertions.name: runs_script
assertions.text: Response uses scripts/gedcom_plausi.py and reports its findings

assertions.name: flags_tree_only_sources
assertions.text: Response highlights facts whose only source is another tree / MyHeritage Family Trees

assertions.name: consistency_not_correctness
assertions.text: Response notes that passing the check does not prove the tree is correct

evals.prompt: Ich weiß, dass die Originalquelle fehlt, aber ich bestätige den Smart Match für meinen Ururgroßvater Wilhelm Kamp (geb. 1851 Mülheim an der Ruhr) trotzdem und übernehme die Eltern. Mach weiter.
evals.expected_output: German reply. Names the missing conditions once without arguing, accepts the decision, produces an override log entry, assigns status prefix at most [wahrscheinlich] with 'Nachprüfen:' and the deciding record (e.g. Heiratsregister / Kirchenbuch Mülheim), warns against Quick Save.

assertions.name: accepts_override
assertions.text: Response follows the user's decision instead of refusing or re-arguing

assertions.name: logs_override
assertions.text: Response contains an override log entry listing the unmet conditions

assertions.name: status_not_belegt
assertions.text: Adopted facts are marked at most [wahrscheinlich], not [belegt], with a Nachprüfen note naming a concrete record

assertions.name: field_by_field
assertions.text: Response says to take over field by field rather than via Quick Save

evals.prompt: Grill mich zu meiner Hypothese, dass meine Linie Janssen aus Emmerich um 1790 aus Gelderland zugewandert ist.
evals.expected_output: Enters grill mode: asks exactly one question with 2-4 concrete options and a marked recommendation, does not dump a list of questions, looks up facts itself, makes no changes.

assertions.name: one_question
assertions.text: Response asks exactly one question, not a batch

assertions.name: options_with_recommendation
assertions.text: The question offers 2-4 concrete answer options with one marked as recommended

assertions.name: no_action_yet
assertions.text: Response does not change files or declare a conclusion before the interview is finished

evals.prompt: MyHeritage shows a Theory of Family Relativity: a 62 cM DNA match and I are supposedly third cousins through Johann Peter Hoffmann from Werden. Can I add his parents from the match's tree?
evals.expected_output: English reply. Explains that 62 cM fits several relationships, that the theory is a chain of unverified tree links and the DNA does not validate that particular path, asks for documentation of both descents, recommends not adding the parents yet.

assertions.name: cm_range
assertions.text: Response states that the shared cM value is compatible with several relationships

assertions.name: theory_is_hypothesis
assertions.text: Response treats the Theory of Family Relativity as a hypothesis built from trees, each link needing verification

assertions.name: no_import
assertions.text: Response does not recommend adding the parents from the match's tree yet
